correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 the neighborhoods N(a_i)={a_{i-1},a_{i+1},b_i} and N(b_i)={b_{i-1},b_{i+1},a_i} give the complete common-neighbor conflict graph. The explicit n-parity cyclic ordering proves H_n is C_(2n)^2 for odd n and two copies of C_n^2 for even n; this covers n=3,4. Open packings correspond exactly to independent sets. Selecting k vertices around a squared cycle requires k cyclic gaps >=3, and m/k times the weak-composition count yields m/(m-2k) binomial(m-2k,k). This proves every coefficient and the six-residue extremal count for all n. The direct neighborhood checker enumerated 1,398,080 vertex subsets across n=3..10, an independent cyclic-column transfer agreed through n=40, explicit graph edge verification agreed through n=40, and the extremal residues agreed through n=150. Finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This result replaces a known maximum-size number with the entire labelled set-count distribution for a canonical infinite 3-regular graph family. The explicit parity-sensitive auxiliary-graph isomorphism is structural and reusable for weighted independent sets and sampling: odd prisms yield one cycle square, even prisms yield two. The sharp six-residue multiplicities vary from constants 3 and 9 to quadratic and quartic formulas; these counts are not determined by published even-n maximum-size identities. The even-class size deficit and six distinct multiplicity regimes show mathematically nontrivial behavior.
